summary.oneLiner: Skipper is a manufacturing-led, globally-qualified transmission-tower/structures play riding India's multi-year grid-capex super-cycle, with record order book and operating-leverage-driven margin expansion, momentarily throttled by export (Middle East) disruption and a CEA-induced FY26 bidding lull that is expected to rebound sharply from FY27.

one-line thesis: Skipper is a manufacturing-led, globally-qualified transmission-tower/structures play riding India's multi-year grid-capex super-cycle, with record order book and operating-leverage-driven margin expansion, momentarily throttled by export (Middle East) disruption and a CEA-induced FY26 bidding lull that is expected to rebound sharply from FY27.
financial scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | FY26 (full year) | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 1,666 cr (record qtr) | +29.4% | INR 5,552.8 cr (record) | +20% |
| — Engineering rev | INR 1,248 cr | +33% | INR 4,359 cr | +24% |
| — Polymer rev | — | — | INR 507 cr (crossed INR 500 cr 1st time) | strong vol growth (~40% vol) |
| EBITDA | INR 173.4 cr | +40.2% | — | — |
| EBITDA margin | 10.4% (vs 9.6%) | +80 bps | 10.3% | ~+50 bps |
| PAT | INR 75.6 cr | +70% | INR 207.3 cr (record) | +42% |
| PAT margin | 4.5% | — | 3.7% | — |
| Finance cost % sales | 3.3% (vs 4.4%) | improved | 3.9% | improved |
| Order book (closing) | — | — | INR 8,501.9 cr (record) | — |
| Annual order inflow | Q4 inflow INR 1,029 cr | — | INR 5,678 cr (record) | — |

Return ratios FY26: ROE 14.1% (vs 12.3%); ROCE ~21% (stable); Debt/EBITDA 1.6x; Debt/Equity 0.62x.
One-offs / quality: Trade receivables ~doubled to INR 1,485 cr — flagged by analyst. Mgmt: ~INR 260 cr received 1-2 April (slipped past March cut-off, technical), domestic rev +45% YoY (longer realization cycle than exports) plus GST; claims no sticky debtors, INR 600-700 cr already realized in April.
guidance (verify next quarter — fy27):
- **Revenue growth: 15%** for FY27 (conservative, on elevated base) — driven down by export weakness + low FY26 inflow.
- **PAT/bottom-line growth: ~30%** for FY27 — explicitly stated as resultant of EXISTING order book quality, NOT dependent on new wins.
- EBITDA margin: no exact number; aspirational long-term 12%; expect continued improvement despite "challenging year with increased costs."
- Capex FY27: ~INR 250 cr (similar to prior years).
- Long-term: return to 20-25% revenue growth from FY28 once exports reopen and bidding normalizes.
- New 75,000 MT capacity commissions Q2 FY27, meaningful utilization from Q3 FY27; adds ~INR 1,000-1,200 cr annual revenue at full utilization.
order book & pipeline:
- Closing order book INR 8,501.9 cr; mix 90% domestic / 10% export.
- Bidding pipeline >INR 33,000 cr (~60-65% domestic, 35-40% export); historical conversion 20-25%.
- Large multimillion-dollar order won from a leading North American utility (developed-market breakthrough).
- 25 active PGCIL projects; executing ~5,000 ckm of EHV & HVDC.
- Domestic book "predominantly Power Grid"; <10% from private players (targeting Tata Power, Adani, Resonia).
- FY26 bidding lull: key projects deferred into FY27 — Krishnagiri REZ Phase 1; Vizag-Kakinada-Tuticorin; 800 kV Rajasthan Barmer (HVDC). PGCIL guides INR 90,000 cr-1 lakh cr annual bids; PGCIL capex INR 35k cr FY26 → INR 37k cr FY27 → INR 45k cr FY28. Awarding to approach FY25 levels from FY27.
segment / subsidiary:
- **Engineering** (~78% of FY26 rev): core T&D, leading growth, ~100% EHV (400/765/800 kV), almost all sales now T&D (legacy low-margin non-T&D phased down → margin uplift).
- **Polymer** INR 507 cr, +~40% volume but value growth lower (commodity deflation); margins still low single-digit; double-digit aspiration as revenue approaches INR 700-1,000 cr; still Eastern-region-concentrated, slowly expanding North/West.
- **Infra / non-T&D**: now only ~14% of order book; order book declined INR 2,000 cr → ~INR 1,000 cr over 6-7 quarters; largely BSNL O&M; de-emphasized.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Substations**: entering as new vertical (~4 HV substations under execution), doubles TAM — lines are ~50% of transmission capex (~INR 50,000 cr), substations the other 50%; mgmt claims substation margins similar to Engineering at project level.
- **HVDC**: qualified, executing a couple of projects; 15,500 ckm of HVDC TBCB projects expected FY28-FY32.
- **Monopoles**: higher-margin, dual test-bed enables lattice + monopole testing.
- **Export developed markets**: North America order won; Europe, Australia in discussions; long-term target 25% then 50% export mix.
- **Intrastate TBCB** & eventual lower-voltage (132/220 kV) TBCB as new demand pool.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Operating leverage at >85% utilization is the core margin lever; incremental volume = higher margin.
- Better product mix (more 765 kV, HVDC, monopoles, T&D-only) lifting margins; aspirational 12% EBITDA.
- 100% indigenous raw material — no import/supply disruption.
- Healthy mix of firm-price (with commodity buffer) and variable-price contracts → confident of absorbing input inflation; this underpins the 30% PAT-growth guide despite RM inflation.
- Freight: only ~10% export book + FOB/CIF mix + force-majeure renegotiation → ocean-freight spike not a margin risk.
capex / expansion:
- Capacity to reach 450,000 TPY by June '26 (75,000 TPY spillover slipped from Mar to Jun).
- Further +75,000 TPY in FY27 and +75,000 TPY in FY28 → ~600,000 TPY by FY28.
- FY27 capex ~INR 250 cr. New 75k line live Q2 FY27, ramp by Q3.
- Test Bed 2 commissioned — only company globally with dual test beds at one location; highest-capacity in world (record 293-ton tower tested; 350-ton planned next month) → shorter engineering/testing lead time = competitive moat.
- SAP S/4HANA RISE go-live; plant audits cleared across NA, Middle East, LatAm, Australia, Europe.
capital allocation:
- Conservative leverage: Debt/Equity 0.62x, Debt/EBITDA 1.6x stable; improving working-capital efficiency.
- Capex steady ~INR 250 cr/yr (self-funding from improving cash generation); no dividend/buyback discussed on call.
risks & watch-items:
- **Exports / Middle East**: order inflow & execution hit by geopolitics; timing of recovery unclear — primary reason for soft FY27 guide.
- **Trade receivables doubling** to INR 1,485 cr — monitor realization despite mgmt reassurance.
- **ROW / forest clearances**: on-ground execution slippage vs scheduled timelines.
- **Critical-equipment shortage** (transformers, HVDC) — global, throttles system commissioning & bidding pace; not within Skipper's control.
- **Bidding timing risk**: FY27 awarding ramp is the key catalyst; any further CEA/PFC-REC delay pushes the re-acceleration.
- Polymer margins stuck in low single digits; sub-scale vs national players.
- Sea-freight inflation slowing export customers' decision-making.
management quality / tone: Confident, detailed, candid. Quantified guidance (15% rev / 30% PAT), explicitly conservative and willing to flag exports/ROW as headwinds rather than hide them. Strong command of sector structure (TBCB, PGCIL share, NEP numbers). Consistent multi-year narrative (manufacturing-led platform). Credibility supported by record metrics across the board.
non-obvious takeaways:
- 30% PAT growth is "locked" from existing order book quality, decoupled from new-order timing — a high-conviction earnings floor regardless of bidding lull.
- The FY26 bidding slowdown was deliberate (CEA "purposely held back" due to backlog + equipment shortage), not demand weakness — implies pent-up FY27-28 surge, not structural decline.
- Substation entry quietly doubles TAM (lines 50% → +substations 50%); margins claimed similar, not dilutive as analyst assumed.
- Dual test-bed + world-record tower testing is a genuine, hard-to-replicate qualification moat for large international (developed-market) orders.
- Receivable spike is largely a March-end technical slip (INR 260 cr) + domestic-mix shift, not deterioration — but worth verifying next quarter.
- Non-T&D/infra now negligible (14%, mostly BSNL O&M) — company is essentially a pure-play T&D structures manufacturer now.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary stock(s) | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| India grid-capex super-cycle (NEP, RE evacuation, PGCIL capex INR 37k→45k cr) | SKIPPER · 538562; Power Grid / PGCIL (code unverified) | — | Record bidding pipeline, FY27 award ramp; largest tower-structure TAM. High |
| FY27 bidding rebound after deliberate FY26 lull | SKIPPER · 538562 | — | 20-25% conversion on INR 33,000 cr pipeline; book to grow. High |
| Substation TBCB opportunity (other 50% of capex) | SKIPPER · 538562 | — | New vertical, similar margins, ~4 HV substations executing. Med |
| HVDC build-out FY28-32 (15,500 ckm) | SKIPPER · 538562; Power Grid (code unverified) | — | Qualified, executing HVDC; Barmer 800 kV bidding FY27. Med-High |
| Middle East / export geopolitics & sea-freight | — | SKIPPER · 538562 (export segment) | Export inflow & execution hit; drives 15% conservative FY27 rev guide. Med |
| Critical-equipment (transformer/HVDC) global shortage | Transformer makers e.g. Transformers & Rectifiers, Voltamp (codes unverified) | SKIPPER · 538562 (execution delay) | Bottleneck delays line commissioning & curtails bidding; benefits scarce-equipment suppliers. Med |
| ROW / forest-clearance delays | — | SKIPPER · 538562; all T&D EPC peers (codes unverified) | On-ground execution slips vs schedule across industry. Med |
| Private-developer share gains (Tata Power, Adani, Resonia) | Tata Power, Adani Energy Solutions (codes unverified) | PGCIL (share dilution risk) | Rising private TBCB participation; Skipper targeting <10%→higher private share. Low-Med |

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "India's largest (top 10 globally) integrated T&D tower structures manufacturer" and "Most preferred EPC contractor and supplier of Transmission tower of HVDC / High Voltage Transmission line Projects", with "Experienced Promoter with 4 decades of expertise".
- "First Indian company to design and supply transmission monopoles to North America"; "Strong international presence in over 50+ countries"; one of the suppliers to the South America transmission market under an "exclusive agreement with a major TSO signed in 2014".
- Deck argues entry barriers are rising: the shift to HVDC, 1150 kV ultra-high-voltage corridors and storage integration means "Higher technical complexity - fewer qualified players", with the industry "moving from commoditized to high-engineering - favors established players like Skipper".
- Highest-ever closing order book of Rs 92,166 Mn (also stated as Rs 9,217 Cr), up 8.4% over the March 2026 level of Rs 85,019 Mn; deck cites an "Order book to revenue ratio of 1.7 x on FY26 Revenue".
- Order book split given as T&D Domestic 80% / Export 9% / Non T&D Domestic 11%; separately a geographical breakup of Domestic 91% / Export 9%.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- 30% PAT growth is "locked" from existing order book quality, decoupled from new-order timing — a high-conviction earnings floor regardless of bidding lull.
- The FY26 bidding slowdown was deliberate (CEA "purposely held back" due to backlog + equipment shortage), not demand weakness — implies pent-up FY27-28 surge, not structural decline.
- Substation entry quietly doubles TAM (lines 50% → +substations 50%); margins claimed similar, not dilutive as analyst assumed.
- Dual test-bed + world-record tower testing is a genuine, hard-to-replicate qualification moat for large international (developed-market) orders.
- Receivable spike is largely a March-end technical slip (INR 260 cr) + domestic-mix shift, not deterioration — but worth verifying next quarter.
- Non-T&D/infra now negligible (14%, mostly BSNL O&M) — company is essentially a pure-play T&D structures manufacturer now.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body: - First file for this ticker — no prior quarter baseline in repo. Baseline established at Q4 FY26: order book INR 8,501.9 cr, FY26 rev INR 5,552.8 cr, EBITDA margin 10.3%, PAT INR 207.3 cr; capacity heading to 450k TPY (Jun'26) → 600k TPY (FY28); FY27 guide 15% rev / 30% PAT.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Guidance] FY27 guidance reaffirmed at ~15% revenue growth and ~30% PAT growth, with a "12% +" long-term EBITDA margin aspiration; FY'27 expected to be H2-weighted on capacity ramp-up, with targeted export order inflows to grow by over 50% versus last year.
- [Export risk] Exports declined ~50% YoY to Rs 1,620 million (vs Rs 3,257 million), "impacted by geopolitical developments in West Asia, leading to delays / temporary holds" — a live concentration risk against the export-scaling strategy.
- [Technology record] "Set a new industry benchmark by Prototyping and testing World's heaviest transmission tower, weighing 320 MT surpassing our own past held record of 293 tons".
- [Order wins] "Secured two (2) prestigious 765 Kv line projects from a reputed domestic developer in the state of Maharashtra"; FY'26 saw the "highest ever annual order inflow of Rs 56,780 mn".
- [Industry frame] Sourced from CareEdge and the CEA plan: global grid investment of USD 3,053 bn in CY24-29 (vs USD 1,644 bn CY19-23); India NEP capex outlay of Rs 9.2 tn during FY22-32 on high voltage (>220kV); CEA plan for >900 GW non-fossil integration by 2035-36 implies ~Rs 7.9 lakh crore, 1,37,500 circuit km of lines and 8,27,600 MVA of substation capacity.
